title: RAGAS metrics
summary: RAGAS defines LLM-judged metrics for RAG: faithfulness and answer relevancy for the generator, context precision, context recall and entities recall for the retriever, and noise sensitivity for how irrelevant context corrupts answers. Each has inputs it needs and a blind spot.
useIf: You need readable RAG metric definitions and have few or no relevance labels.
avoidIf: You expect a faithfulness score to prove the answer is true, or you compare scores across different judge or embedding models.

explain.md: RAGAS splits RAG quality into the retriever half and the generator half, and scores most items with an LLM judge [[r20]]. Read each metric by what it divides by what.

explain.md: Map symptoms to metrics. Low **context recall** says the evidence never reached the prompt: fix retrieval. High recall with low **faithfulness** says the generator ignored or invented beyond the context. High **noise sensitivity** says irrelevant chunks led the model to wrong claims. Low **answer relevancy** says the response drifted off the question.

Run each metric where its inputs exist. Faithfulness and answer relevancy need only the question, the response and the retrieved contexts (plus an embedding model for relevancy), so they also work on live traces. Context recall, context entities recall and noise sensitivity need a reference, so they belong to the offline golden set. Because an LLM judge and an embedding model produce the numbers, pin both and re-baseline when either changes.

explain.title: API and naming drift
explain.md: ragas 0.4.3 was released on 2026-01-13. The docs show the collections API (`ragas.metrics.collections`, `ascore` and `score`). The legacy `SingleTurnSample` API is deprecated in 0.4 and removed in 1.0. The docs title says Response Relevancy while the class is `AnswerRelevancy` [[r20]].

Foundry's evaluators label the same two halves a **precision aspect** (Groundedness) and a **recall aspect** (Response Completeness, preview, needs `ground_truth`) [[r4]]. DeepEval offers Contextual Relevancy, Precision, Recall, Answer Relevancy and Faithfulness [[r28]]. Names differ across tools, so compare definitions, not labels.

pitfalls.symptom: Faithfulness is 0.95 but the answer is wrong
pitfalls.cause: The retrieved document was wrong or outdated, and the answer matched it
pitfalls.fix: Pair faithfulness with context recall and a reference-based correctness check

pitfalls.symptom: Scores jumped after a library upgrade
pitfalls.cause: Metric implementation or default prompts changed, or the judge model changed
pitfalls.fix: Pin the library, the judge and the embedding model, and re-baseline after any change

pitfalls.symptom: Answer relevancy is high for a confident wrong answer
pitfalls.cause: It measures topical match to the question, not accuracy
pitfalls.fix: Never use it as a correctness gate

scenarios.title: Hallucination complaints, labelled references
scenarios.situation: Users report invented details in a policy assistant. A reference answer exists for 300 test questions. The team suspects retrieval but cannot prove it.
unknowns: Is context recall high or low?
Do wrong claims appear in the retrieved text?
scenarios.question: Which metrics split the cause?

options.name: Context recall, faithfulness and noise sensitivity on the 300 items
options.why: Low recall points to retrieval, high recall with low faithfulness points to the generator, and noise sensitivity shows whether irrelevant chunks mislead.
options.tradeoff: Three judged metrics cost judge calls for 300 items.

options.name: Answer relevancy alone
options.why: It measures topical match and ignores both facts and context.
options.tradeoff: Useful for catching answers that dodge the question.

options.name: Faithfulness alone
options.tradeoff: It cannot say whether the context itself was complete or right.

flips.then: Use faithfulness and ContextUtilization, and start writing references for the worst cases.

flips.if: Context recall is high and faithfulness is high
flips.then: Check that the reference and corpus are not outdated.

scenarios.takeaway: Pair a generator metric with a retriever metric to localise the fault.

scenarios.title: Production monitoring, no references, tight budget
scenarios.situation: A support assistant handles 50,000 conversations a day. There are no reference answers. Finance caps judge spend, and security allows reading only a redacted sample.
unknowns: What sampling rate fits the budget?
scenarios.question: Which RAGAS-style metrics do you run on live traffic?

options.name: Faithfulness and answer relevancy on a sampled, redacted slice
options.why: Both run without references and flag unsupported or off-topic answers at a cost you control by sampling.
options.tradeoff: They cannot tell when retrieval missed the right document.

options.name: Context recall and noise sensitivity on all traffic
options.why: Both need references that live traffic lacks, and full coverage breaks the budget.
options.tradeoff: They suit the offline golden set where references exist.

options.name: Sample 1% for human review only
options.why: High-quality labels and no judge cost.
options.tradeoff: Slow, and low coverage of rare failures.

flips.then: Increase the sample and add ContextUtilization for retrieval health.

flips.if: Traffic is sensitive and cannot be read
flips.then: Score metadata and safety signals only.

scenarios.takeaway: Without references, use the reference-free metrics and sample.

quiz.q: What does RAGAS faithfulness actually measure?
options: Whether the answer is true in the world
Whether the retrieved chunks were ranked well
Whether the answer addresses the question
Whether the response's claims are supported by the retrieved context
quiz.explain: Faithfulness divides context-supported claims by total claims. It checks consistency with context, not truth, ranking or relevance to the question.

quiz.q: Context recall is 0.35, faithfulness is 0.92. Where do you look first?
options: Retrieval: the needed evidence rarely reaches the prompt
The embedding model used for answer relevancy
quiz.explain: Faithful answers over missing evidence mean the generator is following weak context. Low recall means the reference claims are not in the retrieved context.

quiz.q: Which RAGAS metrics need a reference answer? Select all that apply.
quiz.explain: Context recall, noise sensitivity and the reference variant of context precision need a reference. Faithfulness needs only the input, response and retrieved contexts.

flashcards.back: Claims in the response supported by the retrieved context divided by total claims in the response. It checks consistency with context, not truth.
An LLM generates N questions (default 3) from the response. The score is the mean cosine similarity of their embeddings to the user question. It needs an embedding model and ignores facts.
The share of response claims that are wrong against the reference yet attributable to retrieved context. Lower is better. Modes: relevant (default) and irrelevant.
